NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.

The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

Thulasimathi Murugesan

Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comeback

Two more gold medal opportunities await

Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan won silver in the women's singles SU5 event. The 24-year- old lost to China's Yang Qiuxia 18-21, 11-21 in the final. She is still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.

Article Title: Jesus Owono handed 12-match ban after Jesus de Miguel's death; FC Andorra goalkeeper yet to decide on return
Article Text:
Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono (AP Photo)

Owono yet to decide on return after 'most difficult days of my life'

Tribute to CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel. (Reuters Photo)

De Miguel's family thanks supporters after fundraising campaign

Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match suspension by the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee following the on-field collision that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.Owono, who plays for Spanish second-division club FC Andorra, collided with De Miguel during their league match on November 2. The Tenerife forward was rushed to hospital and admitted to intensive care but died the following day.The federation's disciplinary committee imposed the maximum sanction under Article 102 of the Royal Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary code, which deals with violent conduct against an opponent during play resulting in serious injury. The suspension also carries the associated fines prescribed under Article 52."The referee's own description makes it possible to appreciate the particular seriousness of the action, both because of the way it was carried out, with the leg raised, and because of the forcefulness of the impact, which the referee expressly described as excessive," the committee said."It is public knowledge that the tragic outcome of the events was the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," it added, saying that the particular seriousness of the case justified "the imposition of the sanction at its maximum level".While the disciplinary action has now been announced, Owono's immediate future in football remains uncertain, with the 25-year-old yet to decide when, or whether, he will return to competitive action.FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said on Thursday that the club would give the goalkeeper the time and space needed to make that decision following the tragedy."What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to him," Manso said at a press conference on Thursday."We will give him space so that he feels completely free to make any decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return."Manso added that Owono was spending time with his family, friends and partner as he dealt with the aftermath of the incident."It is a very complicated situation to manage," the manager said, adding that the goalkeeper would decide his next step "when he feels it is appropriate and when he feels genuinely ready to take a decision like that".Owono had earlier withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea's squad for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month. The goalkeeper, who has 47 international caps, had described the ordeal as "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement released through his club.The Equatorial Guinea Football Federation also said he was experiencing profound sorrow and grief following De Miguel's death.Meanwhile, De Miguel's family issued a statement on Thursday through the Spanish Players Association, thanking those who had extended their support following the Tenerife forward's death.A crowdfunding campaign organised by third-tier club Hercules forward Fran Sol for the family had raised €213,160."We would like to express our heartfelt thanks for all the expressions of affection and support we have received," De Miguel's family said."We have been deeply moved to see so many of you rally behind this initiative."The family also thanked Sol for setting up the campaign, with the proceeds intended to support De Miguel's relatives.FC Andorra are scheduled to travel to Almeria on Saturday for their first fixture since the tragedy.
Article Summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed 12-match suspension by Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee. Owono collided with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during their league match on November 2. De Miguel was taken to hospital but died the following day. The suspension carries the associated fines prescribed under Article 52.

Article Title: No number 10 jersey, stands not full: Messi-less Argentina brought down to earth by Uruguay
Article Text:
Lionel Messi

Argentina's first match in the post-Lionel Messi era ended in defeat, with Uruguay beating the world champions 2-1 in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday.Playing their first match since Messi's retirement from international football in early October, Argentina were unable to begin the new chapter with a win under coach Lionel Scaloni.Uruguay took the lead in the 48th minute through an own goal by Leonardo Balerdi. Five minutes later, Maximiliano Araújo doubled the visitors' advantage under new coach Diego Forlán.Julián Álvarez pulled one back for Argentina in the 73rd minute, but the hosts could not find an equaliser.The match, known as the clásico rioplatense, marked the beginning of a new phase for Argentina following Messi's international retirement. Scaloni, who led the team to the 2022 FIFA World Cup title, extended his contract until 2030 earlier this week.Messi's absence was the biggest talking point ahead of the match. The 39-year-old brought an end to his international career last month after an emotional farewell friendly against Benin, having represented Argentina in 207 matches and scored 125 goals.The impact of his absence was also visible in the stands, with La Bombonera falling short of a sellout crowd, something rarely seen during Argentina matches.Although most supporters wore Argentina's traditional blue-and-white jersey with Messi's No. 10 on the back, Scaloni decided not to give the shirt number to another player. The coach said he was yet to decide who would succeed Messi and preferred to leave the number vacant for now, as there was no obligation to assign it.On the field, Argentina continued to dominate possession but lacked the attacking threat and creativity that Messi brought to the team in the final third. Neither Nicolás Paz nor Thiago Almada managed to fill that gap.Argentina will look to return to winning ways when they face Costa Rica in Córdoba on Tuesday. Uruguay, meanwhile, will host the Dominican Republic on the same day.
Article Summary: Argentina's first match in the post-Lionel Messi era ended in defeat. Uruguay beat the world champions 2-1 in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday. Lionel Messi retired from international football in early October.
